newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba Pool earnings fall 45 pct on low volume.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba Pool earnings fall 45 pct on low volume.

text.p: Manitoba Pool Elevators' net earnings in fiscal 1996 (Aug/July) fell 45 percent because of lower grain shipments, capital restructuring and member loans, MPE's president and chairman Charlie Swanson said.
"A principal factor was a decline in grain receipts which resulted in reduced revenues," MPE president and chairman Charlie Swanson said in a release Tuesday.
MPE is Canada's sixth largest grain handling firm and posted net earnings in fiscal 1996 of C$5.545 million compared with C$10.051 million in 1995, MPE's annual report showed.

Manitoba's production of the six major grains and oilseeds in crop year 1995/96 (Aug/July) was 94 percent of the previous year's output at 7.12 million tonnes compared to 7.58 million, Statistics Canada and United Grain Growers figures show.
MPE held a 50 percent share of grain handling in Manitoba in each of the last four fiscal year, the report showed.
Grain receipts at primary country elevators dropped nine percent in fiscal 1996 to 2.61 million tonnes from 2.87 million the previous year.
Receipts at MPE terminals in Thunder Bay, Ontario, dropped 40 percent to 1.04 million tonnes from 1.73 million tonnes.
MPE handled 17 percent of grain shipments in Thunder Bay and closed one of its two grain terminals there June 15, 1996.
"Another significant factor (in lower earnings) was a provision for restructuring which reduced earnings by C$11.7 million," Swanson said.
The restructuring was set to cover the cost of shutting down primary and terminal elevators as part of MPE's cost cutting strategy.
MPE reduced its network of primary elevators by 5.3 percent to 124 from 131 while overall capacity fell 4.0 percent to 520,000 tonnes from 542,000 tonnes.

"The company paid out C$4.5 million to members as repayment of patronage loans and withholding taxes paid on behalf of members based on the previous year's earnings. A further C$3.8 million in patronage loans is expected to be repaid during 1996/97," Swanson said.
MPE is a cooperative owned by about 16,000 farmer-members.
